steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The nervous system has two main parts: the Central Nervous System (CNS = brain + spinal cord) and the Peripheral Nervous System (PNS = all other nerves connecting the CNS to the body).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The PNS has two divisions: the Somatic Nervous System (controls voluntary movement of skeletal muscles and receives sensory information) and the Autonomic Nervous System (controls involuntary functions like heart rate, digestion, breathing).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Autonomic Nervous System has two branches: the Sympathetic Nervous System (activates the body for action - increases heart rate, dilates pupils, releases adrenaline - the 'fight-or-flight' response) and the Parasympathetic Nervous System (calms the body - decreases heart rate, constricts pupils, promotes digestion - the 'rest and digest' response).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The fight-or-flight response: when a threat is perceived, the amygdala signals the hypothalamus, which activates the sympathetic nervous system and the endocrine system (adrenal glands release adrenaline). This prepares the body to fight or flee.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Describe the structure of the nervous system, distinguishing between the CNS and PNS. | Explain the fight-or-flight response, including the role of the sympathetic nervous system. | Evaluate the usefulness of the fight-or-flight response in modern life.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: CNS: brain and spinal cord - processes information and coordinates responses. PNS: all nerves outside the CNS - connects the CNS to limbs and organs. Somatic: voluntary control (moving your arm). steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: CNS = brain + spinal cord. PNS = everything else. Somatic = voluntary. Autonomic = involuntary. Sympathetic = FIGHT or FLIGHT (activates). Parasympathetic = REST and DIGEST (calms). Fight-or-flight: amygdala -> hypothalamus -> sympathetic -> adrenaline.
